name: 1634 Prairie Avenue — stone-front house, the north half of the pair with 1636, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), stone (blue) front, attached to 1636'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-2350 (piece 2 of T-2346) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the main body is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K02 stone street front, K03 brick side and rear walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 stone front bay, K10 bracketed street cornice — under the flat roof K05 learned for the stone-front rowhouse (T-2349), which K01 now builds as k01.roof.flat. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '3B', brick with a stone front, attached to 1636, the traced main body and the stone bay before it) through the T-1840 census. Its south wall is the party wall it shares with 1636 and is built blank. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1634-stone-front-flat-2350. The sheet's three-storey rear wing waits for T-2347. No photograph, plate or description of 1634 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1634 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1634 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The south-west corner of the K01 footprint, kept from the draft: the rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 30.750, v -3.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 2.46 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.58 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle inside the traced main part s20fp-1634-b1 p2 (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328), kept from the draft (13.75 m deep, 6.75 m along the front; the part's rectangles cover 86% of its fill). The trace also draws the stone front bay (p1, rectangle u 14.25-15.5, v 0-3.0: the draft's r3), built here as a K08 bay, and a three-storey wing behind the rear wall (u -6.5-0, v -0.5-4.25: the draft's r2), which waits for T-2347.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three full storeys over a basement.

construction.note: The sheet colours the street front blue (stone) on a brick (pink) house: the register reads 'brick with stone front'.

principal_floor_m.note: The draft rules' principal floor, 1.4 m over the basement, inside the K01 contract's 0.8-1.8 m; 1628's.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first: 1628's, inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's starting ranges. The wall head stands at 12.3 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1612's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

stone_front.note: Brownstone, K02's brown sandstone, smooth-dressed over two rusticated base courses up to the area lights' heads. The sheet says only stone; the brown is chosen on the Prairie library's text record cgn-1634-text (Chicagology's 1634 page), which quotes the Inter Ocean of 10 September 1890 calling the house 'the brown stone mansion No. 1634'. That record is not a source here, so the attribute stays reconstructed. No corner returns: the south corner is the party wall with 1636, and K02 returns the south corner only.

street_front_trim.note: K09 cornice-hood lintels on the two lower storeys and K01's flat stone lintel on the low third, 1628's.

wall_head.note: The bracketed street cornice the register's stone-front family carries: K10's timber brackets and bed moulding under the flat roof's cornice box, along the street front alone (the side walls rise into parapets).

roof_form.note: The stone-front family's flat roof behind its cornice, as the draft rules drew it (k01.roof.flat, from K05's k05.roof.flat_parapet, T-2349): a tin deck falling to the rear wall, a coped parapet on each side wall and a blocking course over the front. No source reads this roof.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall to the rear fascia, 2 degrees: the K05 variant's own, inside its declared 1-5 degree band.

eave_overhang_m.note: The street cornice box projects 0.6 m from the stone, the brackets' reach with room to the fascia, as 1628's eave.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the pair's north (outer) end, the draft rules' row: 1636 mirrors it to the south.

front_bays.note: Two bays across the 6.75 m front, south to north: the stone bay's on the south, and on the north the door with a window a storey over it.

bays.note: The sheet's stone front bay (s20fp-1634-b1 p1, 3.0 m along the front at its south end, 1.25 m out) as K08's rectangular bay, 2.6 m by 1.2 m (the kit's plan, which a record may not resize), three storeys of stone with a sash to the front and one in each cheek, under a low tin hip that stops under the cornice's brackets (its third storey is 2.0 m to the bay's eave). Its centre is 0.25 m north of the sheet's, to leave K01's 0.3 m pier at the corner.

side_bays.note: None: the south wall is the party wall with 1636 and is built blank.

north_bays.note: Three windows a storey along the north wall, front to rear as K01 reads that wall, one to each room of a three-room-deep house; the wall faces 1630's side yard.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall, north to south. The southern one stands where the sheet's rear wing joins and becomes the opening into it when T-2347 stands the wing.

basement_lights.note: Area lights under the principal windows, 0.65 m high so that two rusticated base courses and the coping reach their heads (K02's course range).

roof_covering.note: K04's flat-seam painted tin, the covering of a low-slope deck, with painted tin flashing; no caps, since a flat deck has no hip or ridge.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks against the south party wall, where a rowhouse's flues rise, over the walls between front, middle and back rooms; 0.9 m above the deck's high line. No source reads this house's chimneys.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a straight stoop; the front yard is the draft's street line (24.61 m from the rear corner) less the 13.75 m body.
